TCL._comment: Chennai. From the client's own 13 stated rules plus a seven-day sample week (data/raw/source_workbooks/chennai_client_structure.xlsx, sheets 'Sheet1' and 'TCL'). The site serves Saturday AND Sunday on reduced menus, which is what most of the rules below are about. TWO of the thirteen are NOT rules at all and need no config: 'in healthy rice we will serve only Curd Rice daily' is already what the `curd_rice` slot does (its pool is the `is_curd_rice` flag, and chennai.json's `curd_rice_is_a_staple` lets the same dish recur), and the client's kuzhambu and kootu requirements are about which SLOT holds what — see the two `_needs_db_change` notes. ONE STATED RULE CONTRADICTS THE SAMPLE: the client says 'welcome drink will be buttermilk twice a week', but all five sampled drinks are buttermilks (BUTTERMILK / SAMBARAM / INJI MOORU / BUTTERMILK / NEER MOORU — sambaram and neer mor both carry `is_buttermilk`). The stated rule is what is configured, since that is what the client wrote down; if they meant 'plain buttermilk twice and a variant otherwise' the fix is to narrow the selector to the one dish.
_needs_db_change: serve_weekends = true. The client works Saturday and Sunday; the row says false, so today only Mon-Fri is planned and every weekday_restriction below that names sat/sun is inert.
categories += white_rice, papad. The sample serves steamed rice on all six non-Saturday days and fryums/appalam every day, and both are CONST slots the counter does not declare.

rules._comment: 'in dal need to give only Kootu item'. Chennai's kootus are `sub_category = kootu` and — as of scripts/chennai_client_pools.py — `course_type = dal`, which is the position the client's own grid puts them in. A one-slot component with count 1 IS 'this slot must be a matching dish' (note 20).
rules.name: tcl_dal_is_a_kootu

rules._comment: '2 flavoured rice one will be biryani daily and other will be south flavoured rice'. The two components must not be satisfiable by ONE dish, or the second cell goes free: six of Chennai's veg biryanis are `cuisine_family = south_indian`, so a plain 'south' selector would be met by the biryani itself. The south side therefore selects the three non-biryani south rice sub_categories (`south_one_pot_rice`, `south_rice_bath`, `south_veg_pulao` — 29 rows, none of them a biryani).
rules.name: tcl_rice_is_a_biryani_and_a_south_rice

rules._comment: Saturday serves ONE rice ('only one south flavoured rice'), so the second rice cell stands down for that day alone — `slot_indices` skips one expansion instead of the whole family, which is what a bare slot_day_restriction would do. The composition above then places the south rice in the surviving cell and its biryani component drops (a component relaxes rather than forcing INFEASIBLE), which is exactly the intent.
rules.name: tcl_one_rice_on_saturday

rules._comment: Sunday serves white rice and no flavoured rice at all ('on sun chapathi, white rice, samabar, rasam, dal, veg gravy, welcome drink, salad and papad only').
rules.name: tcl_no_flavoured_rice_on_sunday

rules._comment: 'in salad need to give only KUZHAMBU item'. The client categorises a kuzhambu as a SALAD, not a gravy — their words — and the sample week proves the two are different rows rather than one mislabelled: Sunday's stated menu lists 'veg gravy' and 'salad' separately, and the grid serves VEG KURMA beside KARA KUZHAMBU. scripts/chennai_client_pools.py re-files Chennai's twelve kuzhambus `veg_gravy` -> `salad` accordingly, so this composition has a pool to draw on; before that the salad pool held none and the rule was unsatisfiable. A one-slot component with count 1 IS 'this slot must be a matching dish' (note 20). Selected by NAME because `sub_category` is `mixed_veg_curry`, which also holds the kurmas the veg_gravy slot serves, and because the ontology spells the word five ways.
rules.name: tcl_salad_is_a_kuzhambu

rules._comment: Saturday serves one veg gravy. Retained at slot_counts.veg_gravy == 1 this is inert, and harmless: it only fires if the counter is ever given a second gravy expansion.
rules.name: tcl_one_veg_gravy_on_saturday

rules._comment: 'liquid based sweet 3 a week'. `exact` counts DAYS, and dessert runs Mon-Fri only (Saturday and Sunday drop it), so this is 3 of the 5 dessert days. Chennai carries 17 liquid sweets after scripts/chennai_client_pools.py, against ~10 the 20-day cooldown needs at this rate.
rules.name: tcl_liquid_sweet_three_days

rules._comment: 'welcome drink will be buttermilk twice a week'. See the _comment at the top: the sample week disagrees with this, serving a buttermilk-family drink on all five days. Configured as stated.
rules.name: tcl_buttermilk_twice_a_week

rules._comment: 'in non veg main egg based to be served on mon, Wednesday and Friday'. The sample fills Tuesday and Thursday with chicken (CHICKEN GRAVY, CHETINAD CHICKEN MASALA), so those two days name chicken rather than merely excluding egg — with one nonveg cell a per-weekday component determines the day outright.
rules.name: tcl_nonveg_egg_mwf_chicken_tue_thu

rules._comment: 'no biryani in non veg main to be served'. A ban, so `max: 0` — the counter's biryani is the veg one in its rice slot.
rules.name: tcl_no_nonveg_biryani

rules._comment: 'no item like baby corn, panner and mushroom will given on sat and sun'. Counted across every slot, because the point is the weekend plate. Baby corn matches on the dish NAME for the reason chennai.json's baby_corn_weekly explains (`key_ingredient = baby_corn` is the de-facto default for a mixed salad). `forbidden_weekdays` degrades rather than fails if a slot's whole pool is premium on that day.
rules.name: tcl_no_premium_veg_on_the_weekend

rules._comment: Saturday's menu is 'chapathi, only one south flavoured rice, healthy rice, veg gravy, welcome drink, veg dry and papad only' — so salad, dal, sambar, rasam, dessert and non-veg all stand down. Sunday's is 'chapathi, white rice, samabar, rasam, dal, veg gravy, welcome drink, salad and papad only' — so veg dry, dessert, curd rice and non-veg stand down there. Six rules, one per slot, each listing the days it DOES run.
rules.name: tcl_no_dal_on_saturday

rules._comment: Salad appears in Sunday's stated list and not Saturday's. The salad IS the kuzhambu (see tcl_salad_is_a_kuzhambu), so this is what stands the kuzhambu down on Saturday — the sample's Saturday column serves VEG KURMA and no kuzhambu.
rules.name: tcl_salad_not_on_saturday

rules._comment: Curd rice is in Saturday's list ('healthy rice') and not Sunday's.
rules.name: tcl_curd_rice_not_on_sunday

rules._comment: Dessert and non-veg appear in neither weekend list.
rules.name: tcl_dessert_on_weekdays_only

_disable_why.mixedveg_pulao_biryani_weekly: chennai.json caps mixed-veg pulao/biryani at one DAY a week in the rice slot, and every one of Chennai's 22 veg biryanis carries `is_mixedveg_biryani`. TCL serves a biryani in its first rice slot every day, so the cap and the client contradict each other outright.
_disable_why.kootu_twice_weekly: chennai.json caps kootu at two days a horizon, on the reading that a kootu is an everyday Tamil dish rather than a treat. TCL's dal IS the kootu, every day. This is the note-9e conflict shape and it went undetected: the city rule is slot-less, so `days_forced_by_composition` was asked about `base_slot=None`, matched no composition, and /diagnose answered would_succeed while the solve came back INFEASIBLE. Fixed in slot_composition_rule.py; the disable is still the right call for this client.
_disable_why.salad_is_not_a_kuzhambu: TCL is the ONLY client that asked for a kuzhambu in its salad slot, so the city ruleset keeps kuzhambus out of the salad by default and TCL switches that off. Without the city default the re-file leaked into five other Chennai counters' salads; without this disable, TCL's own stated rule is unsatisfiable. The pair is what makes 'only in the mentioned clients' true.
